checks: erasure requires the exact original deployment/user/device/epoch namespace
numeric, zero, padded and overflowing epochs do not authorize cleanup
boxed identifiers cannot authorize deletion by implicit string coercion
all original devices and epochs, including legacy and retained archives, belong to the same personal account
every maintained payload holder, including Blob queues and failed-cleanup markers, is in the erasure inventory
snapshot, schema and migration stages require an exact namespace and an actual UUID stage
original operation suffixes never change the namespace owner
other users, deployments, origins and nonpersonal sources remain separate
data-rights receipts, shared authentication history and global facts are never blanket-deleted
the original auth fence is retained while payload holders are removed
array keys, invalid namespaces and owner-like substrings cannot trigger deletion
the permanent write barrier is shared by old epochs and retained archives
a matching username alone cannot establish original local ownership
scope: actual production key/ownership rules only; no claim of transaction, erasure or UI execution
